description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between "Co-occurrence Number" and "ACC (%)" for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale with labeled tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to 85, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5 units (60, 65, 70, 75, 80). All six methods are represented by solid lines that demonstrate a steady upward trend across four distinct data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, increasing from approximately 61.2 at the first data point to 66.8 at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from roughly 62.4 to 68.3. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, growing from about 64.5 to 70.1. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at approximately 65.8, rising to 71.2 at the second data point, and ending at 73.9. The "MEMIT" method is shown as a purple line with pentagon markers, increasing from roughly 66.3 to 72.6. Finally, the "ROME" method is depicted by a green line with square markers, starting at the highest initial value of approximately 72.2, rising to 75.9 at the second data point, and ending at 77.7 at the final x-value.
